children: Shares of Aster DM Quality Care Ltd. declined on Monday, September 28, even as brokerage firm Motilal Oswal initiated coverage on the stock, indicating an upside potential of 20% as part of its "base case".
Motilal Oswal initiated coverage on Aster DM with a "buy" rating and a target price of ₹910 per share.

According to the brokerage, the Aster DM Healthcare-QCIL merger creates one of India's largest hospital platforms, Aster DM Quality Care, with 39 hospitals and 10,600 operational beds across 28 cities. The platform has capacity to scale beyond 15,000 beds by the financial year 2030 through a balanced brownfield / greenfield / asset-light approach.

A cluster-led strategy anchors the growth story, with Kerala's mature, high-margin base complemented by a faster-growing Karnataka / Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh / Telangana footprint, providing both earnings stability and a long growth runway, it added.

The QCIL merger meaningfully deepens regional diversification, bringing a complimentary set of hospital networks under one roof and creating a genuinely pan-India platform with stronger potential for cross-cluster referrals, as per Motilal Oswal.

Prior to the merger, Aster DM showcased a growth-plus-margin story, with revenue in financial year 2025 and 2026 rising to ₹4,100 crore and ₹4,600 crore, while margins expanded by 300 basis points and 90 basis points respectively. That momentum continued in the June quarter as well, with revenue growth of 22% and Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) growing by 27% from last year.

Motilal Oswal expects Aster DM's revenue, EBITDA and Profit After Tax (PAT) to grow at a Compounded Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 19.5%, 25% and 33% respectively over financial year 2026-2029, reaching figures of ₹13,200 crore, ₹3,070 crore and ₹1,650 crore respectively, which will be aided by procurement, clinical and cost synergies.
Bull case scenario

In its bull case scenario, Motilal Oswal assumes 12-month forward EBITDA of ₹2,910 crore and assigns a 30x enterprise value (EV) / EBITDA multiple, implying a target price of ₹1,110 per share, indicating a 46% upside.

The bull case factors in faster earnings growth, driven by the successful integration of the QCIL merger, accelerated realization of procurement and operating synergies, stronger occupancy and average revenue per occupied bed (ARPOB) improvement across the combined network, and higher contribution from medical value and high-end specialties, it said.
Bear case
The bear case scenario assumes 12 month forward EBITDA of ₹2,490 crore and a lower 25x EV/EBITDA multiple, implying a target price of ₹700, which indicates a downside of 8%.
It factors in slower-than-expected synergy realization, delayed ramp up of new capacities, weaker occupancy gains, and persistent cost pressures following the merger.
Key risks
Motilal Oswal mentions the following key risks for the Aster DM stock in its note:
QCIL integration and delays in synergy realization could weigh on margins.
Expansion delays could defer growth and weaken return on capital employed (RoCE).
Regulatory changes and price caps could pressure profitability.
Stock reaction
Of the 15 analysts who have coverage on the Aster DM Quality Care stock, 13 have a "buy" rating and one each have "hold" and "sell" ratings.
Shares of Aster DM Quality Care are trading 1.4% lower at ₹748.45. The stock is up 23% so far this year.

title: Motilal Oswal 'bull case' projects 46% upside for this chain of hospitals
